comparison: Both evaluate phase separation claims (C30-C35, C36-C37, C40). OpenEval finds comprehensive support from phase diagrams, microscopy, and ionic strength data. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the phase separation findings and experimental approach, noting 'both negative polymers drive the formation of metastable protein/polymer condensates.'

Both address maturation behavior claims (C43-C51). OpenEval finds strong support from turbidity, ThT fluorescence, and FRAP data. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'polyP-driven condensates form more gel- or solid-like structures over time' and accept the divergent maturation behaviors without critique.

Both evaluate structural claims about polyP effects (C57-C62, C63-C71, C74). OpenEval finds support from CD spectroscopy. Peer reviewers explicitly state authors 'observe the formation of polyproline II-like structures' and accept the mechanistic insights from CD and SVD analysis.

Both address structural characterization claims (C63-C71). OpenEval finds support from SVD and FTIR analysis. Peer reviewers accept the polyproline II-like structure formation and do not challenge the spectral decomposition methods.

Both evaluate DNA-induced condensate behavior (C78, C81-C84). OpenEval finds support from turbidity and microscopy showing uniform behavior across variants. Peer reviewers note 'DNA-driven condensates tend to dissipate over time' and commend the charge-equivalent DNA controls.

Both address DNA control experiments (C87-C92). OpenEval finds support from FRAP, FTIR, and CD data ruling out concentration effects. Peer reviewers affirm the DNA controls 'further reinforcing the polymer-specific effects of polyP.'

Both evaluate FruR validation claims (C93-C100). OpenEval finds support from comprehensive FruR experiments strengthening generalizability. Peer reviewers acknowledge the FruR extension but note 'some discrepancies between protein systems remain unresolved,' expressing uncertainty about generalizability.

Both address the key comparative conclusion (C101-C103). OpenEval finds strong support from comprehensive data. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'polyP distinguishes among protein conformational ensembles' but note 'lack of a consistent trend,' expressing uncertainty about polyP as a reliable probe.

Both evaluate DNA vs. polyP comparison (C103, C7). OpenEval finds support for differential behavior. Peer reviewers affirm DNA shows 'minimal structural effects' and accept the dissolution behavior after DNA controls addressed concerns.

Both address thermodynamic mechanism claims (C104-C106, C75-C76). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are plausible but speculative interpretations requiring validation. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the metastability and phase transition interpretations as consistent with experimental data.

Both evaluate structural flexibility mechanism (C107-C109, C33, C104). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are chemically reasonable but require direct structural studies. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the proposed role of polyP flexibility in driving differential behavior.
Both address methodological claims about OD and ThT (C110-C111). OpenEval finds support from literature and temporal measurements. Peer reviewers accept these technical details without challenge.

Both evaluate speculative implications (C112-C115, C116-C120). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable hypotheses but not directly tested. Peer reviewers SUPPORT these as valuable contributions to understanding bacterial stress responses.

Both address biological implications (C116-C120). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to C120 being explicitly speculative. Peer reviewers SUPPORT these implications as contributing to broader understanding of polyP assembly processes.

Both evaluate synthesis of structural and kinetic data (C74-C77, C75-C76). OpenEval finds strong support from combined measurements. Peer reviewers accept the thermodynamic interpretation of metastability and divergent maturation behaviors.
Both address early phase separation claims (C36-C37, C40-C42). OpenEval finds strong support from microscopy and FRAP. Peer reviewers affirm the phase separation findings and experimental soundness.

Both evaluate the role of conformational state (C41-C42, C8, C77, C101-C102). OpenEval finds support for charge composition being insufficient. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the consistency of trends linking phase transitions to conformational ensembles.
Both address main findings in abstract (C2-C4). OpenEval finds these accurately reflect detailed results. Peer reviewers affirm the phase separation and metastable condensate formation findings.

Both evaluate abstract claims about structural insights (C5-C6). OpenEval finds support from comprehensive data. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the polyproline II-like structure formation observations.
Both address DNA minimal effects claim (C7). OpenEval finds support from comprehensive data. Peer reviewers affirm DNA shows minimal structural effects compared to polyP.

Both evaluate abstract claim about conformational ensemble role (C8). OpenEval finds support from comprehensive data. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the consistency of this relationship across protein systems.
